result: For finite-dimensional multipartite systems, finite lambda, additive Hermitian local Q, and [H0,Q]=0, grand-canonical/field thermal states are related by a reversible product filter. Thus full separability, k-producibility, cut-PPT and cutwise Schmidt number have exactly field-independent status. This extends to nonuniform weights iff the weighted charge commutes. Rossignoli-Canosa 2013 gives XXZ cutwise PPT/negativity prior art; family-specific full-separability-boundary priority remains UNKNOWN. A finite two-qubit XX example proves noncommuting staggered-field entanglement status can change.
limitations: Does not determine the zero-field numerical boundary.
Zero-temperature or singular infinite-parameter limits are outside the reversible-filter theorem.
Targeted primary-source audit, not an exhaustive historical priority review.
Reduced-state entanglement and entanglement magnitudes are not implied invariant.
